stem: An order-processing fleet's size should track the backlog of pending work rather than each worker's CPU utilization, since individual work items vary widely in processing time.

choices.text: A target tracking policy on CPU utilization
A scheduled scaling policy for predictable daily peaks
A target tracking policy on the queue's ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric
A target tracking policy on network in/out

rationale: Scaling on the SQS queue's ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric ties the fleet's size directly to the backlog of pending work, which is what this scenario asks for when item processing time varies too much for CPU to be a reliable proxy. CPU utilization target tracking scales on how busy each worker already is, not on how much work is waiting, so it does not track backlog directly. A scheduled policy scales on a fixed clock-time pattern, not on the actual amount of pending work, which does not fit workloads with unpredictable, variable-duration items. Network in/out target tracking reflects data transfer volume, not the number of queued work items waiting to be processed.
